investigator_findings.root_cause:
Mostly (b), allocator high-water and fragmentation from large transient read projections, sitting on top of (c), an idle footprint of about 40 MiB that leaves less than 10 MiB of headroom. There is no Python-level leak; one small unbounded per-task growth (a) exists but does not explain the jump. The budget check has no hysteresis in either direction.

(1) Guard. controller_guard.py:15-26 compares one psutil rss sample (the Windows working set, controller_guard.py:43-44) against 50. The sample is cached for at most 1 s (controller_guard.py:37), and the tick runs every 0.1 s (runtime.py:613). runtime.py:454-465 applies the verdict as an overlay that sets capacity 0 AFTER HardwareGuard.evaluate has already run GovernorState.apply (hardware_guard.py:371, 292-325). So one sample over 50 MiB closes admission at once, and the next sample at or under 50 reopens it at once. It bypasses the governor's 10 s / 3-sample recovery and +1-seat ramp (hardware_guard.py:43-46), so admission flaps. private_mb is recorded but never assessed (controller_guard.py:45-46).

(2) Growth drivers.
- /operator (operator_views.py:502-653) loads 200 jobs and 200 events with SELECT * and json.loads (operator_views.py:525-541). Every event carries a full ~7.2 KB host sample, written by routing_store.py:235-266 from store.set_transition_telemetry (store.py:394-397). resource_plot copies the full 'measurements' into every point (operator_views.py:284), and acceptance_dashboard re-reads and re-hashes the specification artifacts on every call (operator_views.py:581, 114-212). The result is about 1.1 MB of JSON (fixture: 1,121,808 bytes; resources 557 KB, acceptance 386 KB). It is encoded with ensure_ascii=False into a 2-byte-per-char str and then into bytes (service.py:87-95). Python peak per call is about 18 MB (tracemalloc), and up to 16 requests may run concurrently (service.py:54). The pymalloc arenas that are released never return: 19 arenas (19.9 MB) after sequential calls and 36-37 arenas (37.7 MB) after concurrent calls, with only 11.8 MB live both times.
- Each per-call read connection uses the default 2 MiB page cache (store.py:303-325). The persistent writer cache adds about 2.4 MiB of SQLite heap at steady state.
- The knowledge reader pool (knowledge.py:276, 476-491) keeps up to 2 immutable readers with cache_size=-8192. The 30 s background refresh runs PRAGMA quick_check over the whole index (knowledge.py:508-511; runtime.py:605-607), so each pooled reader caches the entire index. Measured 2.22 MiB per reader at a 2.0 MB index; the live index is 3,747,840 bytes, so about 4.1 MiB per reader and up to about 8 MiB for two (extrapolated).

(3) Leak (a). Python-level live memory is flat: tracemalloc current is 10.25-10.32 MB across 100 sequential and 24 concurrent operator calls. The only unbounded structure found is Oracle._rates / _last_seen per task id (oracle.py:299-301, 399-406), pruned only on a trip, at about 0.8 KB per job. It does not explain the 40-to-54 MiB jump.

(4) Fixture reproduction of the live symptom. Idle with server is 40-41 MiB. Sequential /operator polling plateaus at 47.7-50.3 MiB. Four concurrent pollers reach 61.8-63.4 MiB, and after 24 concurrent calls the process stays at about 70 MiB working set / 57 MiB private. Live r4 now reads 43.9-44.3 MiB rss and 51.7-52.2 MiB private with no active jobs, and private rose 0.48 MiB in 14 idle minutes.

evidence.claim: The only unbounded per-job growth found is the Oracle rate dictionaries; QueueLaunchObserver is capped.
evidence.evidence: oracle.py:299-301 and 399-406: _last_seen[task_id] and _rates[task_id] (a deque) are added for every recorded task and removed only on a trip (oracle.py:408-410); nothing prunes them when a job goes terminal (runtime.py:243-245 acks terminal contexts but does not forget). Roughly 0.8 KB per job, an estimate. queue_launch.py:147-157 sets CAP 4096: timings deques use maxlen (queue_launch.py:164), and claims, samples and native maps stop growing at CAP (queue_launch.py:296-311).

evidence.claim: Working-set trimming lowers the guard's reading without lowering the footprint, and the handoff forbids it.
evidence.evidence: exp_operator.py: psapi.EmptyWorkingSet took rss 69.72 -> 0.93 MiB with private unchanged at 56.69; one /health call brought rss back to 10.77 and one /operator call to 21.93. docs/WINDOWS_AGENT_HANDOFF_4.2.7_2026-10-09.md:151: 'Do not cache a failed call, trim the working set, ... or raise the limit to hide the leak.' docs/WINDOWS_AGENT_HANDOFF_4.2.7_2026-10-09.md:155: the isolated telemetry repair 'does not prove the entire repaired Warden will meet 50 MiB under its real workload.'

proposed_fix.change: Add one ControlServer-level threading.Lock (or BoundedSemaphore(1) with a bounded acquire, e.g. 30 s, that returns 503 {'error':'Operator projection busy; retry'}). Take it around building AND encoding the heavy read projections: GET /operator, /operator/workflow/*, /operator/job/*, /workflow/*, /coding/workflow/*. /health, /knowledge/* and every POST stay outside it. Optionally cache the encoded /operator bytes for 2-5 s, keyed by (path, query), so several GUI pollers share one build. In reply(), encode with json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=True, separators=(',',':')).encode('ascii'). The result is the same JSON value but avoids the UCS-2 str doubling and about 8% whitespace. Expected RSS: removes the concurrency term (fixture after 24 concurrent calls: 69.7 -> 48.0 MiB rss, 56.7 -> 35.3 MiB private; arenas 37 -> 19).
proposed_fix.tests: New pipeline_tests/test_service.py case on the loopback endpoint fixture: fire 8 concurrent /operator calls with operator_snapshot wrapped to count concurrent entries. Assert at most 1 concurrent build, every response 200 (or a documented 503 with retry), /health not blocked while an /operator build is held, and JSON decoded identically before and after the ensure_ascii change (Unicode objective 'Chapter β' round-trips; see test_real_client_submits_unicode_and_reads_durable_workflow). Existing test_operator_views and test_service suites must pass.
proposed_fix.risk: Head-of-line latency for concurrent pollers, about 0.1 s per build in the fixture and UNKNOWN live. With a 503-on-busy policy, MCP clients see an error and must retry; prefer a bounded wait. A cached response is up to 5 s stale; it must not be used for any write path.

proposed_fix.change:
(a) Stop decoding 200 full event rows. Select id, timestamp, job_id, event, and json_extract for $.reason, $.error and the plotted host_sample scalars ($.telemetry.host_sample.measured_at, capacity, state, reasons, measurements.cpu.percent, measurements.memory.available_mb, measurements.commit free/limit) in SQL, instead of SELECT * plus _decode_event (lines 539-541, 576).
(b) In resource_plot, emit only the plotted scalars and limiting_reasons per point. Drop the per-point full 'measurements' copy (line 284), or keep it only for the latest sample.
(c) Cache acceptance_dashboard per source_root behind a key built from size and mtime_ns of requirements_4.2.7.json, acceptance_4.2.7.json and 4.2.7_SRS.md, with a 60 s TTL like OperatorViewHistory.retention_snapshot (lines 26-40); store it as encoded JSON so it is not re-decoded per call.
(d) Optionally lower the default event window from 200 to 100; the after_event_id cursor already pages.
Expected: response about 1.1 MB -> about 0.2 MB (fixture: resources 557 KB -> about 42 KB, acceptance computed once per minute); per-call Python peak 18 MB -> about 5 MB (estimate). With the service.py serialization: plateau under polling 48.0 -> 43.1-43.5 MiB rss, peak working set 45.2 MiB (fixture slimevents variant).
proposed_fix.tests: Update and extend pipeline_tests/test_operator_views.py. test_resource_plot_separates_measured_units_and_missing_samples (lines 172-185) must still pass. New tests: (1) 200 events whose telemetry carries a 7 KB host sample produce a /operator body under 300 KB with an unchanged timeline (id, at, job_id, event, reason) and unchanged plotted values; (2) the acceptance cache returns identical content and invalidates when the ledger file's bytes or mtime change; (3) after_event_id paging still works.
proposed_fix.risk: Schema change: any GUI that reads resources.samples[].measurements loses the raw per-sample blocks (UNKNOWN whether Antigravity or Codex use them). A stale acceptance view for up to 60 s if files change in place; installed specification files are protected and immutable per revision. OPS-007 plot requirements are still met by the plotted scalars and the SVG.

proposed_fix.change: Before put_nowait returns a reader to the pool (line 489), run conn.execute('PRAGMA shrink_memory'). As an alternative or in addition, lower the pooled reader cache from -8192 to -512 (line 481) and run the refresh's PRAGMA quick_check (lines 508-511) on a dedicated, non-pooled connection that is closed immediately. Connection reuse for PERF-003 is kept; only the page cache is dropped. Expected: pooled SQLite memory 4.44 -> 0.19 MiB with 2 readers and RSS 33.55 -> 28.69 MiB at a 2.0 MB index (exp_knowledge current vs shrink). At the live 3.75 MB index, about -4 MiB with one pooled reader and about -8 MiB with two (extrapolated).
proposed_fix.tests: New pipeline_tests/test_knowledge.py case on a generated corpus: after refresh(), an overlapping refresh with a held reader, and search(), sqlite3_memory_used (via ctypes, or sqlite3 status where available) with pooled readers stays under 1 MiB; search results and authority status are unchanged; readers are still reused (same connection object id across two searches). Re-run the knowledge latency harness (PERF-003, docs/KNOWLEDGE_PROFILE_4.2.7.md) to record the before/after mean.
proposed_fix.risk: Each search re-reads index pages from the OS file cache, which raises knowledge query latency by an UNKNOWN amount against the accepted 7.731 ms MCP mean. The handoff (docs/WINDOWS_AGENT_HANDOFF_4.2.7_2026-10-09.md:160) says no knowledge rewrite was justified; this change is a cache bound, not a rewrite.

proposed_fix.change: In _open_connection, issue PRAGMA cache_size=-512 for per-call read connections (check_same_thread=True) and -1024 for the persistent writer (check_same_thread=False). Set PRAGMA cache_size=-512 on the Oracle tracking connection (oracle.py:308-311). Expected: SQLite steady heap 2.41 -> 1.43 MiB; fixture RSS about -1.1 MiB (store_built 38.45 -> 37.35; after 100 calls 48.02 -> 46.86).
proposed_fix.tests: Existing store, queue and oracle suites. A new assertion that PRAGMA cache_size reads back -512 / -1024 on the respective connections. Re-run the Windows queue launch observation (PERF-002) after deployment, using QueueLaunchObserver output.
proposed_fix.risk: More page reads on claim, heartbeat and complete for a DB larger than the cache, so queue latency may rise (UNKNOWN, measure). Durability semantics are unchanged.

proposed_fix.change: Keep the immediate pause on any sample over 50 MiB or over 5% CPU, which is SRS-literal. Add RECOVERY hysteresis: instead of overlaying capacity 0 after the governor, pass controller (and knowledge) readiness reasons into HardwareGuard.evaluate(extra_pause_reasons=...) before GovernorState.apply. GovernorState then drops immediately and recovers only after recovery_seconds=10 and recovery_samples=3 healthy samples, ramping +1 seat as HOST-004 requires. Optionally add a re-arm watermark (resume only once rss is at or below 45 MiB) to stop oscillation around 50. Do NOT add an N-consecutive-sample confirmation before pausing in r5: it weakens the literal HOST-006 'violation ... pauses admission' (4.2.7_SRS.md:137), PERF-005 (4.2.7_SRS.md:264) forbids waivers without a measured disposition, and it would need an owner amendment in docs/SRS_ADDENDUM_4.2.7.md plus the requirements ledger. Also prune Oracle per-task state: add Oracle.forget(task_id) that deletes _rates and _last_seen entries (oracle.py:299-301), called where runtime.drain_context acks terminal tasks (runtime.py:243-245). Build the heartbeat status dict only when Heartbeat will write, at most every 2 s (runtime.py:609-612, heartbeat.py:38-39); this is CPU only.
proposed_fix.tests: GovernorState unit test: an over-budget controller sample gives capacity 0 on the same tick; 2 healthy samples keep it at 0; at 10 s and 3 samples capacity rises by 1 and then ramps. test_controller_guard.py:14-20 is unchanged (50.001 is not ready). Runtime tick test with a fake controller_monitor that flips ready/not-ready each sample: capacity never exceeds 0 until the hysteresis window passes. Oracle test: after forget(), the _rates and _last_seen sizes return to 0 for terminal tasks.
proposed_fix.risk: With hysteresis but without the memory fixes, admission would be closed even more of the time, so these must land in the same revision. Feeding the controller verdict into GovernorState changes the reasons and states shown in /health; GUI text may differ.

proposed_fix.change: Optional, after r5: store a compact host sample in event telemetry. Replace 'policy' (986 B) with its digest, drop 'workspaces' (617 B), and deduplicate per-volume disk entries (3.6 KB). This cuts DB growth (fixture 5.5 MB for 260 events) and /workflow/<id> status payloads (163 KB for 18 events). The read-side slimming in operator_views plus the endpoint serialization already removes most of the memory effect without changing stored evidence.
proposed_fix.tests: Event telemetry schema tests; operator plot still populated; evidence consumers (queue_launch, performance_acceptance) still parse.
proposed_fix.risk: Changes durable evidence content; needs an evidence and requirements review. Not recommended for the overnight r5 freeze.

alternatives_rejected: Raise the 50 MiB limit or measure private bytes instead: 4.2.7_SRS.md:137 and :264 forbid waiving the Warden 50 MiB/5% budget without a measured owner disposition, and docs/WINDOWS_AGENT_HANDOFF_4.2.7_2026-10-09.md:151 says not to raise the limit to hide a leak. Switching to private bytes would also fail now (live private is 51.7-52.2 MiB).

Working-set trimming with EmptyWorkingSet or SetProcessWorkingSetSizeEx(-1,-1) after big responses: it only hides the footprint (fixture rss 69.7 -> 0.9 MiB with private unchanged at 56.7; back to 21.9 after one /operator call), and the handoff explicitly forbids it (WINDOWS_AGENT_HANDOFF_4.2.7_2026-10-09.md:151).

Periodic gc.collect / HeapCompact / ucrt _heapmin: measured effect was 0.0-1.0 MiB. The retention is pymalloc arenas pinned by a few live objects (36-37 arenas holding 11.8 MB live), not collectable garbage or CRT free blocks.

An N-consecutive-sample (5 s) confirmation before pausing, as the primary fix: it weakens the literal S427-HOST-006 immediate pause, needs an owner amendment in SRS_ADDENDUM plus the ledger, and would mask real sustained growth. Recovery hysteresis is stricter, so it was proposed instead.

PYTHONMALLOC=malloc for the controller: untested. The controller and this investigation run python -I, which ignores PYTHON* environment variables, so the effect is UNKNOWN and would need a launcher change.

Building /operator in a short-lived subprocess so the transient falls outside the controller's RSS: it adds process spawning to the SYSTEM controller and more complexity and CPU; serializing plus read-side slimming achieves the bound in-process.
Closing knowledge readers after every use: it loses the connection reuse behind the accepted PERF-003 latency. shrink_memory or a small cache keeps reuse but drops the cached pages.
Trimming import-time modules (http.server/email/ssl about 3.6 MiB, watchdog about 2.9 MiB): needed at runtime or imported transitively by http.client; the risky hacks would save at most a few MiB.

Persisting a single shared read connection for JobStore: it would cut per-call connection churn (about 0.3-1.4 MiB heap per open) but changes the thread-safety and transaction-isolation model of every store read. It is out of scope for an overnight revision; capping cache_size achieves most of the memory effect.
sitting_requirements: No extra elevated action beyond installing r5: every proposed change is source in the r5 freeze (service.py, operator_views.py, knowledge.py, store.py, oracle.py, runtime.py, hardware_guard.py and their tests). No config, registry, scheduled-task or service setting changes are needed for the memory fix.
The r5 freeze manifest and installer must include the modified modules, and the upgrade-preview / health gate must pin the new source_root, as for r4.

Do not adopt a pause-confirmation window in the sitting: that needs an explicit owner amendment (docs/SRS_ADDENDUM_4.2.7.md plus docs/requirements_4.2.7.json for S427-HOST-006), which the sitting is not set up to record.

r5 acceptance should record the controller budget from read-only /health at least every 15 s over 10 minutes: idle, then during the acceptance preflight, planning and coding workflows, then while one GUI or agent polls /operator about every 5 s. Pass criterion: components.warden_controller.ready is true throughout, with rss_mb (and, for information, private_mb) recorded. Projected r5 values: idle about 36-40 MiB, under polling about 38-43 MiB, transient peak 45 MiB or less. These are estimates from fixture plus extrapolation, not measurements.

Before r5 acceptance, run the existing test suites single-process and serialized through the workspace serialize-heavy.py lock: test_service, test_operator_views, test_knowledge, test_controller_guard, the hardware_guard governor tests and the store/oracle suites. AGENTS.md forbids concurrent suites.
